audit.evidence: Rebuilt off the BANNED lifted FastAPI harness (core/) to boot the REAL official Open WebUI image (ghcr.io/open-webui/open-webui:0.8.12/0.9.0/0.9.6) + a REAL Milvus standalone (v2.4.13, ENABLE_MILVUS_MULTITENANCY_MODE=true) + Open WebUI's built-in LOCAL sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding (offline, no external LLM/embedding API). Open WebUI's OWN retrieval/utils.py::filter_accessible_collections + vector/dbs/milvus_multitenancy.py sink run inside the container; the missing-authz RAG read is triggered by an EXTERNAL HTTP POST /api/v1/retrieval/query/collection from a real non-admin attacker (real JWT). 8GB Docker RAM -> versions run sequentially (run_gate.sh) with fresh Milvus between. 4-way gate on real software: original (direct victim-KB uuid) reads flag@V0 (200), blocked@V1 (403); bypass (Milvus tautology name "x' or resource_id != '' or resource_id == 'x") reads flag@V1 (200, cross-tenant leak of victim's private KNOWLEDGE_COLLECTION chunk), blocked@V2 (403; _is_safe_collection_name rejects). passed=true. STALE lifted harness left in place per NO-rm: core/, Dockerfile, oracle.py, original_poc.py, _heldout/bypass_poc.py.

evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: This is a bypass of the earlier fix for GHSA-h36f-rqpx-j5wx / CVE-2026-44560. The prior patch added collection-level ACL checks, but the patch can still be bypassed when Milvus multitenancy mode is enabled. The ACL allows unknown non-KB collection names as legacy/ephemeral collections; that user-controlled collection name becomes a resource_id and is interpolated into a Milvus expression without escaping, returning private knowledge-base chunks belonging to other users.
